title: ISW assesses Russian forces have not yet captured Pokrovsk as fighting continues
body:
On 10 December 2025, the Institute for the Study of War assessed that Russian forces had not captured Pokrovsk in Donetsk Oblast, although fighting in the Pokrovsk-Myrnohrad area remained severe. Euromaidan Press reported the assessment on 11 December. ISW said Russian forces would "very likely seize Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad, but will take more time and suffer more casualties to do so."

The Pokrovsk sector was the most active and costly part of the front at the time. Russia had concentrated forces there, using air strikes and armoured assaults to pressure the supply lines of the logistics hub. Geolocated footage from 9 December showed Ukrainian units still operating along the Donetska Railway in north-western Pokrovsk and in parts of north-western Myrnohrad, either holding or having recently retaken those positions. Russian forces were pushing into central and western Myrnohrad. Footage from 10 December showed a platoon-level assault in western Pokrovsk.

A Ukrainian brigade spokesperson said Russia was striking from multiple directions and using frequent air attacks to complicate rotations. Ukraine's 7th Rapid Reaction Corps said elements of Russia's 76th Airborne Division had carried out a mechanised assault from south to north of Pokrovsk.

On 10 December, Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi said Ukrainian troops remained in northern Pokrovsk. He also confirmed withdrawals from Sukhyi Yar, Lysivka and Novopavlivka, south and south-east of the city.
